terms.short: The official list of all registered voters in a constituency.
terms.detailed: The electoral roll (voter list) is prepared and maintained by the Election Commission. It lists all eligible citizens who can vote. Revisions happen annually and before elections. You can check your name at voters.eci.gov.in.

terms.short: Electronic Voting Machine — the device used to cast votes.
terms.detailed: EVMs replaced paper ballots in India. They are standalone, battery-operated devices not connected to any network. Each EVM has a ballot unit (for voter) and a control unit (for polling officer). They can record up to 64 candidates.

terms.short: A geographical area that elects one representative.
terms.detailed: India is divided into 543 Lok Sabha constituencies and thousands of state assembly constituencies. Boundaries are redrawn by the Delimitation Commission based on census data to ensure roughly equal population per constituency.

terms.short: A public document outlining a political party's policies and promises.
terms.detailed: Parties release manifestos before elections detailing their agenda if elected. While not legally binding, manifestos help voters compare parties. The Supreme Court has suggested that unfulfillable promises should be avoided.

terms.short: A survey of voters taken immediately after they vote.
terms.detailed: Exit polls predict election outcomes by asking voters who they voted for. In India, exit poll results cannot be broadcast until after the final phase of voting ends, to prevent influencing voters in later phases.

terms.short: None Of The Above — option to reject all candidates.
terms.detailed: Introduced in 2013 by Supreme Court order, NOTA allows voters to express dissatisfaction with all candidates. However, even if NOTA gets the most votes, the candidate with the highest votes among actual candidates still wins.

terms.short: Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail — paper receipt of your vote.
terms.detailed: VVPAT machines print a small slip showing the candidate name and symbol you voted for, visible for 7 seconds through a window. This provides a paper trail for verification. VVPAT slips from 5 random booths per constituency are matched with EVM results.

terms.short: The official responsible for conducting elections in a constituency.
terms.detailed: Appointed by the Election Commission, the RO manages the entire election process in their constituency — from accepting nominations to declaring results. They are typically senior district officials.

terms.short: Rules governing party and government behavior during elections.
terms.detailed: The MCC kicks in from election announcement until results. It prevents the ruling government from making major policy decisions, prohibits use of government machinery for campaigning, and sets rules for rallies, speeches, and advertisements.

terms.short: A method to vote by mail without visiting the polling station.
terms.detailed: Available to armed forces, government employees on election duty, persons with disabilities, senior citizens (80+), and essential services workers. The ballot is mailed to the voter, who marks it and sends it back to be counted.
